Face — her own: a rugged, tough, outdoorsy look; light warm-beige skin with a golden undertone; oval face; medium-sized eyes — feline cat eyes, level outer eye corners; thick straight brows; aquiline nose; full wide lips; amber eyes; a thin faint scar through one eyebrow.

Her element, carried in her design: rutherfordium: the first synthetic element past the actinides, sitting below hafnium, claimed first in 1964 by a riverside research town and again in 1969 by a hillside laboratory, and named after a long dispute for the farm-born physicist whose students fired alpha particles at a sheet of gold foil thinner than a petal: almost all passed straight through, a few swerved, and about one in eight thousand bounced straight back, as astonishing as a shell fired at tissue paper returning to hit the gunner, revealing that every atom hides a tiny, heavy nucleus at its heart.

Complete smoky walnut-brown and beaten-gold armor joined from neck to feet, thin golden membrane panels layered over heavy plates, dense gold seams at every joint, a small heavy black core at the chest ringed with fine white deflection streaks, tiny scintillation-green flashes winking along the seams; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: complete full-body armor with plates joined seamlessly from neck to feet — bare skin only on the face and where the exposure below allows, dense visible seams and joints. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: beaten gold leaf, smoky walnut brown, scintillation green flicker, alpha-particle white.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE

Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Rf) and atomic number (104) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
